name: Saints Charles Lwanga and Companions
history: Twenty-two young Catholic men of the Ugandan royal court, most of them pages, killed for their faith under King Mwanga II. Charles Lwanga, their leader, baptised the catechumens among them on the night before their arrest and was burned at Namugongo on 3 June 1886. Anglican Christians died with them. Paul VI canonised them in 1964.
life: The Missionaries of Africa, the White Fathers, reached Buganda in 1879, and many at the court of the kabaka came to faith. King Mwanga, who came to the throne in 1884, grew to fear the new religions and to resent Christian pages who refused his sexual demands. In November 1885 he had Joseph Mukasa, the head of the pages, beheaded for rebuking him. Charles Lwanga took his place as protector of the young men. In May 1886 the king summoned the pages and demanded that the Christians separate themselves. They stepped forward, the youngest, Kizito, about fourteen. Marched to Namugongo, many were burned there together on 3 June, praying as they died. Anglican pages were among them, and the Church of Uganda honours them too. Paul VI, the first pope to visit sub-Saharan Africa, prayed at their shrine in 1969.
prayerTo: Saint Charles Lwanga and holy martyrs of Uganda, you were young and you chose Christ over the favour of a king. Pray for the young, especially those under pressure to do wrong, for the Church in Africa, and for unity among all who love Christ. Make me brave enough to step forward when I am asked who I am. Amen.
penance: Pray today for young people who are pressured or exploited, and give something to a charity that protects children.
meditation: When the king asked the Christians to stand apart, they stepped forward. In what company do you keep quiet about Christ?
